title: The Hollow Spire
premise: Gideon Sandoval, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead through the relics they leave behind, has survived by staying small in the smuggler's warrens of Thornfell. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone with the gift, Gideon flees with a ragged found family: a disgraced knight, a child who remembers a country that was erased from every map, and a dying dragon whose fire is the last living proof that the vanished kingdom of Vael ever existed. Their only escape lies through a door that exists only in memory—reachable only if Gideon risks hearing the dead of Vael itself, including the voice of the mother who abandoned them. In the end, Gideon chooses to carry Vael's memories into the new world rather than erase them, sealing the door behind them at the cost of their own gift, and the family walks out into a country willing to be haunted.
about_author: Orsen Voss is the pen name of a former stonemason who spent a decade restoring cathedral gargoyles before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about laborers, exiles, and the stubborn afterlives of forgotten places from a farmhouse at the edge of a mountain range they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the smuggler town of Lowmark, Gideon carves a dead woman's story into her femur while her daughter listens, establishing how bone-carving preserves the dead's voices. A crown notice nailed to the tavern door announces the Purge of Gifts. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the life Gideon built is already ending.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Witch-hunters arrive in Lowmark led by Inquisitor Halvard Crane, who carries a relic that lets him hear what Gideon hears—a hunter with the gift himself. Gideon burns their most dangerous carvings and prepares to flee. Emotional beat: grief for the dead who will now be silenced twice.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Ser Maren Kestrel's POV. A disgraced knight hiding in Thornfell saves Gideon from a patrol ambush on the mountain road, recognizing the gift because her dead commander speaks to her too. She insists on traveling together. Emotional beat: two guarded people discovering they are not alone in their haunting.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In an abandoned waystation they find Pip, an eight-year-old orphan who draws maps of Vael—a kingdom erased from all records forty years ago—and speaks of it as home. The dragon-fire motif appears: Pip carries an ember-stone that never cools. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear; the child is exactly what Crane hunts.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The party reaches the smuggler city of Gravenhollow to buy passage, finding it half-burned by witch-hunters. Gideon's old fence, Odile, betrays their location to Crane for amnesty. Emotional beat: the cost of trust; nowhere underground is safe anymore.

chapters.title: The Ember That Would Not Die
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Fleeing Gravenhollow, the group shelters in a cave where Pip's ember-stone flares, revealing ancient dragon-script on the walls. Gideon hears the stone speak—a dragon's voice, old and tired, calling itself Ashfall. Emotional beat: awe; the last dragon is not a creature but a witness.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Deep in the mountains they find Ashfall, the last dragon, guttering like a candle, kept alive only by the ember-stone. Ashfall reveals the Door of Vael opens only to those carrying true memory of the kingdom—and Pip's ember is the key. Emotional beat: reluctant hope entangled with terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Crane's Confession
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Interlude chapters shift to the hunter: Crane hears his own dead sister in every relic he confiscates, silencing her voice each time he burns one. He believes destroying the gift is mercy. Emotional beat: the antagonist as tragedy—he is what Gideon could become.

chapters.title: The Road Through Teeth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The party crosses the Serrated Pass with Ashfall too weak to fly, ambushed by bounty hunters. Maren takes a wound protecting Pip and confesses she deserted her post during the Vael purge years ago. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh; redemption must be earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Trapped in a frozen cave-in, Gideon carves the ice-bound bones of Vael's last garrison and hears their final stand—including proof that the crown erased Vael to hide its own betrayal. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose; this history must survive.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Odile intercepts them, torn between her betrayal and love for Gideon; she gives them Crane's route but stays behind to delay him, knowing he'll kill her. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution—some debts can only be paid forward.

chapters.title: The Hollow Spire
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. They reach the Hollow Spire, a tower that stands in both worlds—half ruin, half intact Vael architecture visible only to Pip. Inside, the walls replay echoes of Vael's last day. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place you've never been; Pip finally feels real.

chapters.title: The Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Within the Spire, Gideon hears among the dead a voice they know: their mother, a Vael refugee who abandoned them rather than be caught with a gifted child. Her carved confession reveals she left to lead hunters away. Emotional beat: devastation and release; abandonment re-understood as sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Fire Costs
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Ashfall reveals the truth: opening the Door requires burning the ember-stone entirely—the dragon's death will power it. Pip refuses. The family fractures over whether survival justifies killing their companion. Emotional beat: the cruelest arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Halvard Crane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Crane corners them at the Spire gates, but hearing Vael's dead through its walls breaks his certainty—his sister's voice mingles with a nation's. He wavers. Emotional beat: the hunter's crisis of faith; mercy begins as doubt.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon proposes the forbidden alternative: instead of Ashfall's fire, a gifted carver can open the Door by taking Vael's memories into their own body—but the gift will burn out forever, and the memories may destroy the mind. Emotional beat: terrified resolve; Gideon volunteers before anyone can argue.

chapters.title: The Siege of Memory
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Crane attacks as the ritual begins; Maren holds the gate alone against his soldiers, fighting beside ghosts of Vael's guard who rise to defend their door. Emotional beat: the deserter's redemption—she finally stands where she once fled.

chapters.title: All the Voices at Once
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax. Gideon takes in ten thousand deaths, a whole country's memory flooding through them, while Crane—confronted by his sister's voice within the flood—turns his relic against his own men and dies holding the Spire open. Emotional beat: transcendence through annihilation of self.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The Door opens onto the borderlands beyond the crown's reach. Ashfall, freed from sustaining the ember, flies east to die under open sky. Pip carries the cooled stone—the first thing they've owned that is finished rather than lost. Emotional beat: bittersweet passage; endings that are also beginnings.

chapters.title: A Country Willing to Be Haunted
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the far side, Gideon survives but the gift is gone—the dead are silent, including their mother. They carve Vael's stories into ordinary wood and stone so others can read them without magic. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into vocation; memory outliving magic.

chapters.title: The Family We Carried
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Epilogue-settling chapter: the three build a house in the borderlands, take in other refugees fleeing the Purge, and Maren finally writes to her old order—not asking pardon, only telling the truth about Vael. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into home.

chapters.title: Ember-Stone, Cold
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Final chapter, years later: Pip, now grown, keeps the cold ember-stone on the mantel and teaches younger children the maps of Vael. On the last page, the stone gives one faint pulse of warmth—as if something heard, somewhere, and approved. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the dead are gone from Gideon's ears but alive in the telling.
